Ready

Higher marks = higher notes. Wider marks = longer notes. Shaded spaces = breathe. Empty space = a rest.

Breathe on the last beat of each bar. The piano keeps the pulse.

Ready to sing

No sound?

Check your iPad volume and whether sound is going to headphones or another speaker. If playback stays silent, reset the sound below.

Start with the melody, then try chords only. Sing on a comfortable syllable and choose a key and register that fit your voice. Every study has a full beat or more to breathe at the end of each bar, even with no extra gap selected. Take an easy breath rather than a big gasp. A four-beat count-in starts each session. Tempo and musical setting changes restart from the count-in.

About the music & references

These are original practice motifs built from chord tones, nearby scale notes, and simple rhythms. No song melodies, lyrics, or recordings were used. Short musical patterns can still resemble existing music by coincidence.

Progressions 1–7 follow common schemas and rotations described in Open Music Theory. Progressions 8–9 appear in the Willis Wonderland songwriting handouts (Common Chord Progressions). Progression 10 is demonstrated in Jonny Kaine’s I–IV–vi–V lesson. These references informed the harmony only.

Progressions 11–20 draw on David Bennett’s teaching: Royal Road, Andalusian cadence, and the remaining eight harmonic formulas in Pianote’s David Bennett progression guide. Chords are simplified to triads and placed in four equal bars for singing. The etudes are newly written practice melodies, not Bennett compositions or song transcriptions. This app is not affiliated with David Bennett.
